reason: The cited lines read commit history from a local git.Repo via git log/iter_commits and return it as TextContent, including hashes, authors, dates, and messages, so they support returning repository data that may be non-public. Commit author/message fields are data from the repository and can be controlled by commit authors, so the returned content is untrusted. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution; they invoke a fixed git log operation rather than agent-controlled arbitrary code. They also do not show sending data to an attacker-readable destination or other sink, only returning the result to the caller.
